options.name: init_config
options.description: All options defined here are available to all instances.

options.name: service
options.description:
Attach the tag `service:<SERVICE>` to every metric, event, and service check emitted by this integration.

Additionally, this sets the default `service` for every log source.

options.name: instances
options.description: Every instance is scheduled independently of the others.

options.name: directory
options.description:
The directory to monitor. On windows, escape back-slashes; otherwise the YAML
parser fails (for example, - directory: "C:\\Users\\foo\\Downloads").

options.name: name
options.description: Tag metrics with specified name.

options.name: dirtagname
options.description:
The name of the key for the tag used for the directory, the value is the value of "name" (see above).
The resulting tag attached is "<dirtagname>:<name>".

options.name: filetagname
options.description:
The name of the key for the tag used for each file, the value is the filename.
The resulting tag is "<filetagname>:<filename>". Only used if filegauges is set to true and if the directory
contains 20 or fewer files (including files in sub-directories).

options.name: filegauges
options.description: When true stats are an individual gauge per file (max. 20 files) and not a histogram of the whole directory.

options.name: max_filegauge_count
options.description:
The maximum number of files to track as gauges. The default is 20. This data is collected by recursively
traversing the directory and its subdirectories. Increasing this value may significantly increase host
resource usage (CPU and memory). This is only used if `filegauges` is set to `true`.

options.name: pattern
options.description:
the `fnmatch` pattern to use when reading the "directory"'s files.
The pattern is matched against the files' absolute paths and relative paths in "directory".

options.name: exclude_dirs
options.description:
a list of regular expressions used to exclude directories.
For example: node_modules, vendor

options.name: dirs_patterns_full
options.description:
Make exclude_dirs patterns operate on the full directory path (may be slightly slower).
Setting this option to `false` excludes any directory in the traversal with the provided name.
Setting this option to `true` allows you to specify the absolute path. This ensures multiple directories
with the same name aren't all excluded.

options.name: recursive
options.description: When true, the stats recurse into directories.

options.name: follow_symlinks
options.description:
Follow symlinks when traversing directories.
When `recursive: true` is used, setting `follow_symlinks: false` helps avoid symlink loops.

options.name: stat_follow_symlinks
options.description:
When `true`, the stats are gathered for the files the symlinks is pointing to.
When `false`, the stats are gathered for the symlinks themselves.

options.name: countonly
options.description: When true the stats only count the number of files matching the pattern.

options.name: ignore_missing
options.description: When true the check does not raise an exception on missing or inaccessible directories.

options.name: submit_histograms
options.description: Whether or not to submit histograms.

options.name: tags
options.description:
A list of tags to attach to every metric and service check emitted by this instance.

Learn more about tagging at https://docs.datadoghq.com/tagging

options.name: service
options.description:
Attach the tag `service:<SERVICE>` to every metric, event, and service check emitted by this integration.

Overrides any `service` defined in the `init_config` section.

options.name: min_collection_interval
options.description:
This changes the collection interval of the check. For more information, see:
https://docs.datadoghq.com/developers/write_agent_check/#collection-interval

options.name: empty_default_hostname
options.description:
This forces the check to send metrics with no hostname.

This is useful for cluster-level checks.

options.name: metric_patterns
options.description:
A mapping of metrics to include or exclude, with each entry being a regular expression.

Metrics defined in `exclude` will take precedence in case of overlap.
